title: Mast-o musir
subtitle: Persian yoghurt dip with shallots
excerpt: Mast-o musir is a Persian yoghurt dip made by folding thinly sliced or grated shallots through thick yoghurt and leaving it to rest overnight. The shallots mellow in the yoghurt, losing their raw punch and becoming soft and subtly sweet. It is one of the essential dips of the Iranian table.
sourceNotes: A classic Persian mast (yoghurt dip). Musir refers to a type of wild shallot native to Iran with a slightly stronger flavour than regular shallots; ordinary shallots or the white parts of spring onions work well as substitutes.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Must be made at least 8 hours ahead; overnight is best. Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.

content.text: Mast-o musir is deceptively simple: thick yoghurt, shallots, and salt. But the alchemy happens overnight. The shallots begin the process sharp and slightly harsh. After 8 hours in the yoghurt they have completely changed: soft, almost sweet, and deeply infused with whatever complexity they started with.

In Iran, musir refers to a wild shallot with a slightly more pronounced flavour than the cultivated shallots sold in UK shops. Regular shallots are a good substitute; spring onion whites and banana shallots also work well. The key is to slice them very thin so they soften fully.
Use the thickest yoghurt you can find. Greek yoghurt works well; strained labneh gives an even richer base. The dip should be thick enough to hold a spoon upright.

items.prepNote: very finely sliced or grated on the coarse side of a box grater

content.text: Mix the yoghurt, shallots, and salt together in a bowl. Stir well. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, and preferably overnight. The shallots will soften and their flavour will mellow considerably into the yoghurt.
Taste after chilling and add more salt if needed. Spoon into a shallow bowl. Drizzle a little extra-virgin olive oil over the surface and scatter dried mint on top if using. Serve cold.

rows.symptom: Shallots still taste sharp after chilling
rows.cause: Not sliced thin enough or chilled too short a time
rows.fix: Slice as thin as possible and leave overnight. A coarser grate also softens them faster.

rows.cause: Yoghurt too thin or shallots released water
rows.fix: Use thicker yoghurt next time. If too thin, strain through a muslin cloth for 30 minutes in the fridge.

rows.cause: Salted before chilling then not retasting
rows.fix: Always taste after chilling; the shallots draw salt from the yoghurt as they sit. Add salt cautiously at the start.

content.text: Add a small amount of crushed dried rose petals for a floral note that is distinctly Persian. For a sharper result closer to the original wild musir flavour, use half shallot and half spring onion white. Some versions include dried dill.
Mast-o musir must be made at least 8 hours ahead and keeps for 3 days in the fridge. It gets better for the first 24 hours as the shallots continue to soften.

Mast-o musir is part of the spread that appears at every Persian meal alongside the main dishes and rice. The mast family of dips includes mast-o khiar (yoghurt and cucumber) and various herb or spinach versions. They are eaten throughout a meal with bread, as a condiment with rice, and as a starter dip.
